1. (Original) A method for generating a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules used to train a molecular properties model, comprising: obtaining a set of property measurements for a plurality of molecules, wherein each measurement assigns a value for a property of interest relative to a single molecule; selecting ordered tuples of molecules, from the plurality, wherein the molecules, in an ordered tuple of molecules, are ordered relative to one another and the property of interest; and combining the selected ordered tuples of molecules to form the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules.

2. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein selecting ordered tuples of molecules further comprises: applying at least a selection criteria to the plurality of molecules to determine which ordered tuples of molecules, from a set of all possible tuples of molecules, to include in the pseudo-partial ordering.

3. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the ordered tuples of molecules are assigned a weighting value.

4. (Original) The method of claim 2, wherein the selection criteria are selected from: determining whether a relative magnitude in the property measurements for the molecules, is above a selected threshold; determining whether an absolute difference in magnitude, in the property measurements for the molecules is above a selected threshold; and determining whether the probability that the measured values fall outside any experimental error intervals is above a selected threshold.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the ordered tuples of molecules used to form the pseudo-partial ordering contain two molecules, a first molecule and a second molecule.

6. (Original) The method of claim 5, wherein the property of interest assigns a discrete value indicating the presence, or absence, of the property of interest for a given molecule, and wherein the first molecule is assigned a discrete value indicating the presence of the property of interest for the first molecule, and the second molecule is assigned a discrete value indicating the absence of the property of interest for the second molecule.

7. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the molecules included in at least one ordered tuple of molecules represent the same physical molecule, and wherein the property of interest is measured relative to different substituent groups of the same physical molecule.

8. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the molecules included in at least one ordered tuple of molecules represent different possible representations of the same physical molecule.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein a molecule in an ordered tuple is selected from a plurality of virtual molecules, or wherein the ranked order for an ordered tuple is determined using virtual data.

10. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules is represented as a set of ordered pairs, ordered tuples, permutations or cross-products of molecules.

11. (Currently Amended) A computer-implemented method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: obtaining a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; generating, by at least one processor of a computer, a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm; providing the pseudo partial ordering of molecules to the selected machine learning algorithm; and executing, by the at least one processor, the selected machine learning algorithm using the pseudo partial ordering, wherein executing the selected machine learning algorithm trains a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model.

12. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the molecular properties model generates predictions related to a property of interest selected from at least one of a pharmacokinetic property, pharmacodynamic property, physiological or pharmacological activity, toxicity or selectivity; a chemical property including reactivity, binding affinity, pKa, or a property of a specific atom or bond in a molecule; or a physical property including melting point, solubility, a membrane permeability, and a force-field parameter.

13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a classification learning algorithm __configured to be executed on the at least one processor__.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a kernel based learning algorithm __configured to be executed on the at least one processor__.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a variant of a Boosting algorithm, RankBoost algorithm, Alternating Decision Trees algorithm, Support Vector Machines algorithm, a Perceptron algorithm, Winnow, a Hedge Algorithm, decision trees, neural networks, genetic algorithms, genetic programming or any modifications thereof modified to process the pseudo partial ordering of ranked pairs, __wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is executed on the at least one processor__.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, an area above, or below, a receiver operator characteristic curve, __and wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is executed on the at least one processor__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, a function of the rank ordering of molecules in the pseudo partial ordering, __and wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is executed on the at least one processor__.

18. (Original) The method of claim 11, further comprising, determining an accuracy of the prediction for the additional molecule by carrying out laboratory experimentation using physically existing samples of the additional molecule, or by performing a research study using physical samples of the additional molecule.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein generating the representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules comprises: __using the at least one processor to__ generate a vector representation of the molecules, wherein the vector representation is configured to encode the structure of the molecules included the pseudo-partial ordering; or __using the at least one processor to__ generate an n-point pharmacophore representation of the molecules included in the pseudo-partial ordering.

20. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein a threshold value or cutoff molecule is selected for the molecular proprieties model and used to create a classification model.

21. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein the at least one additional molecule comprises two or more additional molecules, and wherein the prediction comprises a ranked ordering of the two or more additional molecules, relative to one another and to the property of interest.

22. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are alternative representations of the same physical molecule and the property of interest is a property of the alternative representations.

23. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are encoded to represent different atoms, bonds or substituent groups of the same molecule and the property of interest is a property of the atoms, bonds or substituent groups.

24. (Original) A method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: obtaining a training set of property measurements for a plurality of molecules, wherein each measurement assigns a value for a property of interest relative to a single molecule; generating a representation of the molecules included in the training set that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm; providing the training set to a selected machine learning algorithm that minimizes a function of the rank order of the molecules in the training set relative to the property of interest; executing the machine learning algorithm to generate a trained molecular properties model; selecting at least one additional molecule; and generating a representation of the at least one additional molecule appropriate for the molecular properties model, wherein the molecular properties model is configured to generate a prediction about the at least one additional molecule regarding the property of interest.

25. (Original) The method of claim 24, wherein the molecular properties model generates predictions related to a property of interest selected from at least one of a pharmacokinetic property, pharmacodynamic property, physiological or pharmacological activity, toxicity or selectivity; a chemical property including reactivity, binding affinity, pKa, or a property of a specific atom or bond in a molecule; or a physical property including melting point, solubility, a membrane permeability, and a force-field parameter.

26. (Original) The method of claim 24, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a variant of a Boosting algorithm, RankBoost algorithm, Alternating Decision Trees algorithm, Support Vector Machines algorithm, a Perceptron algorithm, Winnow, a Hedge Algorithm, decision trees, neural networks, genetic algorithms, genetic programming or any modifications thereof modified to minimize a function of the rank order of the molecules in the training set relative to the property of interest.

27. (Original) The method of claim 24, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, an area above, or below, a receiver operator characteristic curve.

28. (Original) The method of claim 24, further comprising, determining an accuracy of the prediction for the additional molecule by carrying out laboratory experimentation using physically existing samples of the additional molecule, or by performing a research study using physical samples of the additional molecule.

29. (Original) The method of claim 24, wherein generating the representation of the molecules included in the training set comprises: generating a vector representation of the molecules, wherein the vector representation is configured to encode the structure the molecules included the training set; or comprises generating an n-point pharmacophore representation of the molecules included in the training set.

30. (Original) The method of claim 24, wherein a threshold value or cutoff molecule is selected for the molecular proprieties model and used to create a classification model.

31. (Original) The method of claim 24, wherein the at least one additional molecules comprises two or more additional molecules, and wherein the prediction comprises a ranked ordering of the two or more additional molecules, relative to one another and to the property of interest.

32. (Original) The method of claim 24, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are alternative representations of the same physical molecule and the property of interest is a property of said alternative representations.

33. (Original) The method of claim 24, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are encoded to represent different atoms, bonds or substituent groups of the same molecule and the property of interest is a property of said atoms, bonds or substituent groups.

34. (Original) A computer-storage medium containing a program which, when executed by a processor, performs a method for generating a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules used to train a molecular properties model, comprising: receiving a set of property measurements for a plurality of molecules, wherein each measurement assigns a value for a property of interest relative to a single molecule; selecting ordered tuples of molecules, from the plurality, wherein the molecules, in an ordered tuple of molecules, are ordered relative to one another and the property of interest; and combining the selected ordered tuples of molecules to form the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules

35. (Currently Amended) A __non-transitory__ computer-storage medium containing a program which, when executed by a processor, performs a computer-implemented method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: receiving a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; __generating, by the processor, a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm; providing the pseudo partial ordering of molecules to the selected machine learning algorithm; and executing, by the processor, the selected machine learning algorithm using the pseudo partial ordering, wherein executing the selected machine learning algorithm trains a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model__.

36. (Original) A computer-storage medium containing a program which, when executed by a processor, performs a method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: receiving a training set of property measurements for a plurality of molecules, wherein each measurement assigns a value for a property of interest relative to a single molecule; generating a representation of the molecules included in the training set that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm; providing the training set to a selected machine learning algorithm that minimizes a function of the rank order of the molecules in the training set relative to the property of interest; executing the machine learning algorithm to generate a trained molecular properties model; selecting at least one additional molecule; and generating a representation of the at least one additional molecule appropriate for the molecular properties model, wherein the molecular properties model is configured to generate a prediction about the at least one additional molecule regarding the property of interest.

37. (Original) A method for evaluating a prediction about a molecule, generated using a computer-implemented molecular properties model, comprising: receiving the prediction for at least a test molecule generated by the molecular properties model, wherein the molecular properties model is trained using a set of training data, and wherein the training data comprises a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, trained by the steps of: obtaining a set of property measurements for a plurality of molecules, wherein each measurement provides a value for a property of interest relative to a single molecule; selecting at least two molecules to include in the pseudo partial ordering, wherein the pseudo partial ordering of molecules orders each therein, relative to one another and relative to a property of interest; providing the pseudo partial ordering to a selected machine learning algorithm, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is executed using the training data generates the molecular properties model; and determining an accuracy of the prediction for the test molecule by performing experimentation.

38. (Original) The method of claim 37, wherein, determining the accuracy of the prediction for the test molecule comprises: carrying out laboratory experimentation using a physically realized sample of the test molecule.

39. (Original) The method of claim 37, wherein, determining the accuracy of the prediction for the test molecule comprises: performing a research study using a physically realized sample of the test molecule.

40. (Original) The method of claim 37, wherein the determining the accuracy of the prediction comprises: performing a computational simulation configured to model the activity of the test molecule generated by the molecular properties model, relative to the property of interest.
